headline: On well charted growth trajectory, trades inexpensive

highlights: Consolidated topline stood at ₹65,436 crore (up 12% YoY) with steel sales volume of 7.9 MT (flat YoY).
Reported EBITDA stood at ₹10,533 crore with EBITDA margins at 16.1% (up 86 bps QoQ).
Indian operation EBITDA/ton stood at ~₹17.4k vs ₹18.6k in Q1FY27.
PAT (post minority interest) stood at ₹3,666 crore (up 18% YoY).
valuation: Investment Rationale: • India: Capacity expansion to capitalise on rising domestic steel demand : Tata Steel, a century-old steel major, is targeting ~40 MTPA capacity going forward to meet India's growing steel demand, with recently commissioned 0.75 MTPA EAF facility at Ludhiana, taking India crude steel capacity to 27.4 MTPA.
In UK, it is undergoing a 3.2 MTPA Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) project, targeted for commissioning by 2027, supported by a £500 million government grant under £1.25 billion capex.
Additionally, TSL’s cost saving target of ₹7,000 crores in FY27 will act as tailwind going ahead.
watch: Key growth capex projects include: (i) a 4.8 MTPA Neelachal expansion (capex of ~₹33,873 crore); (ii) a 2.5 MTPA thin slab caster & rolling facility; 3) a strategic partnership with Lloyds Metals & Energy to develop an iron ore hub in Gadchiroli, alongside a 6 MTPA greenfield steel plant in Maharashtra.
Investments in securities market are subject to market risks.
